answer: Each agent registers at a unique vertex on the network graph, validated by a cryptographic proof tied to a physical‑world sensor at the juniper ridge data hub. When an agent refers a new node, the protocol issues a reward only if the new vertex’s proof originates from a distinct sensor signature; any duplicate or simulated identity fails the sensor check and yields zero payout. An attacker must therefore acquire costly, geographically dispersed sensor hardware for every fake node, inflating the price of a Sybil attack beyond the reward budget.
